scores.notes: Moment shown (King with notebook, Queen, defiant Alice, animal jury with blank slates, tarts). Card soldiers by the jury box and at right are oblong cards, but at left a page in a red heart tabard stands by the Queen and a spear soldier in a blue cap and card-patterned tabard stands lower left: human soldiers/courtiers.

Jury box upset with sprawling jurors and slates is shown, but the Lizard lies upright on top of the box rim as a crocodile-sized reptile, not head-down inside it. Lower left two wigged men in doublets hold big cards in front of them and a man in a spade-patterned shirt stands in the right crowd (human courtiers). A '3' index is readable on the 3 of hearts. A juror on the floor at centre-left is a jumbled tangle of limbs.

The Caterpillar on the mushroom facing Alice is shown, but the Caterpillar has a fully human old man's face (nose, lips, heavy lids), breaking the animal-face rule. The hookah has no bowl: the hose hangs from the mouthpiece and ends in a floating brass finial that gives off smoke.

Card arches, hedgehogs, flamingo under Alice's arm and the Queen shouting are right, and every soldier is a card. But Alice also holds a wooden croquet mallet in her right hand, which contradicts the live-flamingo mallets, and two White Rabbits stand beside the Queen. Small 'A' indices are visible on the two ace cards at upper left.

The White Rabbit in spectacles reading the paper before the King, Queen and Alice is shown, and the soldiers flanking the throne are cards. But plain humans (an elf-eared man in glasses, a grey-haired woman, a bearded man) sit among and behind the animal jury where the court should be cards and animals. This is a weaker case than tabarded soldiers. The paper on the floor at bottom left has unreadable scribble lines.

The Hatter with teacup and bread-and-butter, the March Hare arm-in-arm with the Dormouse, the trumpeting Rabbit and the owl jury are right, but Alice appears twice (left foreground and centre by the cards). A second hare stands in the back crowd. The card soldiers are cards (mixing suits), but a top-hatted old man and other human spectators fill the crowd.

Raging Queen, uneasy Alice with her flamingo and the Cat appearing are shown (the whole head appears rather than only the grin). The arch soldier bent double in the centre is a human man in a heart tabard. A metal wire hoop stands midground and wooden balls lie by the background players. A second Alice-like girl in a purple dress and apron cowers beside the Queen.

The King peering from behind Alice at the floating Cat head matches the text, but both arch soldiers are human men in card tabards on all fours. A red metal hoop stands midground, and an empty standing coat-shape and a small sign with X marks sit in the background. A tiny girl in a blue dress and white pinafore stands far back, not prominent.

The Cat's head, Alice, and the Queen close behind her listening match the text, but Alice holds a wooden pink croquet mallet with a limp flamingo neck wrapped round the shaft, and the other players swing wooden mallets. The arches are solid horseshoe arches and green faceless humanoids on all fours, and the card soldier at left is a human in a hooded ace-of-hearts tabard.
